title: How Do I Learn? Self-Assessment
description: Assess your transversal competencies: how do you steer your learning, how do you deal with challenges, how do you work with others? Six short self-assessments with sliders – your answers are saved with a date, so you can follow your development in the competency spider web.

learningObjectives: I can explain what transversal competencies are and why they help in every subject.
I can assess my transversal competencies honestly and justify my assessment.
I know where I can follow my development in the competency spider web and how to repeat the assessment.

blocks.title: What this is about
blocks.body:
At school you don't just learn subjects like English or economics – you also learn **how** to learn, work and live together. These skills are called **transversal competencies**: they help you in every subject and far beyond school.

In this module you assess yourself. For each statement, move a slider to the level that fits best: **never · rarely · sometimes · often · almost always · always**.

Three things matter here:

1. **Be honest.** There are no points and no grades here. An honest assessment helps you more than a flattering one.
2. **Your assessment is saved with a date.** If you repeat it later (for example at the end of the semester), you will see your development in the competency spider web on the home page.
3. **Your teacher sees your assessment** when your learning progress is shared – for example via the class folder. They also assess you themselves: comparing the two views is the most valuable part – that's where the best conversations happen.

Take your time. This is not a test – it's a look in the mirror.

blocks.title: How I steer my actions and my learning
blocks.intro: This is about how firmly you hold the steering wheel yourself: making decisions, tackling the important things first, sticking to your goals and completing tasks without being reminded.

blocks.title: How I assess myself and others
blocks.intro: Knowing yourself well makes learning easier: here you assess how well you know your strengths and weaknesses, judge your own work and deal with opinions.

blocks.title: How I deal with challenges
blocks.intro: Difficult tasks, mistakes and setbacks are part of learning. Here you assess how you deal with them – without putting yourself down: this is about looking honestly.

blocks.title: What drives me
blocks.intro: Interest and motivation are your engine. Here you assess how ready you are to take on new things and real effort.

blocks.title: How I work with others
blocks.intro: Learning rarely happens alone. Here you assess how you behave in a group: listening, contributing, keeping to rules, addressing conflicts and respecting everyone.

blocks.title: How I learn and work
blocks.intro: This is about your toolkit for learning: processing information, planning, staying focused, solving problems, managing your time and checking at the end how well it turned out.

blocks.title: What next?
blocks.body:
Done! Your assessments are saved.

- On the **home page** you will find your **competency spider web**: there you can see your assessments as a web – and later also what your teacher has assessed.
- **Repeat this module** every few months. Only several assessments at different points in time make your development visible.
- Talk to your teacher about where your assessments differ – that's exactly where the conversation is most worthwhile.
